verses.text: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, "Why do you just keep looking at each other?"
He went on, "I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we can stay alive and not die."
So ten of Joseph's brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
But Jacob did not send Joseph's brother Benjamin with the others, because he was afraid that something bad might happen to him.
So the sons of Israel were among the many people who went to buy grain, because the famine had reached the land of Canaan too.
Now Joseph was the governor of the land, the one who sold grain to all its people. So when Joseph's brothers arrived, they bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

As soon as Joseph saw his brothers, he recognised them. But he pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them. "Where do you come from?" he asked. "From the land of Canaan," they replied, "to buy food."
Although Joseph recognised his brothers, they did not recognise him.
Then Joseph remembered his dreams about them, and he said to them, "You are spies! You have come to see where our land is weak."
"No, sir," they answered. "Your servants have come to buy food.
We are all the sons of one man. We are honest men. Your servants are not spies."
"No!" he said to them. "You have come to see where our land is weak."
But they replied, "Your servants were twelve brothers, the sons of one man who lives in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no longer alive."
Joseph said to them, "It is just as I told you. You are spies!
And this is how you will be tested. As surely as Pharaoh lives, you will not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.

Send one of you to get your brother. The rest of you will be kept in prison, so that your words can be tested to see if you are telling the truth. If you are not, then as surely as Pharaoh lives, you are spies!"
And he put them all in prison for three days.
On the third day Joseph said to them, "Do this and you will live, because I respect God.
If you are honest men, let one of your brothers stay here in prison, while the rest of you go and take grain back for your starving families.
But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then your words will be proved true, and you will not die." So they agreed to do this.

They said to each other, "We are surely being punished because of our brother. We saw how upset he was when he begged us to spare him, but we would not listen. That is why this trouble has come on us."
Reuben answered them, "Did I not tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen! Now we must pay for his blood."
They did not know that Joseph could understand them, because he was using an interpreter.
He turned away from them and began to weep. Then he came back and spoke to them again. He had Simeon taken from them and tied up in front of their eyes.
Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to put each man's silver back in his sack, and to give them supplies for their journey. After this was done for them,
they loaded their grain on their donkeys and left.
At the place where they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get food for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the top of his sack.

"My silver has been given back," he said to his brothers. "Here it is in my sack!" Their hearts sank, and they turned to each other, shaking with fear. They said, "What is this that God has done to us?"
When they came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they told him everything that had happened to them. They said,
"The man who is lord over the land spoke harshly to us and treated us as though we were spying on the country.
But we said to him, 'We are honest men. We are not spies.
We were twelve brothers, sons of one father. One is no longer alive, and the youngest is now with our father in Canaan.'
Then the man who is lord over the land said to us, 'This is how I will know whether you are honest men: leave one of your brothers here with me, and take food for your starving families and go.
But bring your youngest brother to me, so that I will know that you are not spies but honest men. Then I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in the land.'"
As they were emptying their sacks, there in each man's sack was his bag of silver! When they and their father saw the bags of silver, they were afraid.
Their father Jacob said to them, "You have taken my children from me. Joseph is gone, and Simeon is gone, and now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is against me!"
Then Reuben said to his father, "You may put both of my sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my care, and I will bring him back."

But Jacob said, "My son will not go down there with you. His brother is dead, and he is the only one left. If anything happens to him on the journey you are taking, you will send me, a grey-haired old man, to the grave in sorrow."
